rules.quote: Don’t use exclamation marks in formal content, such as government reports or briefings.
rules.violation_condition: An exclamation mark is used as emphatic punctuation in formal government content.
when: Applies to formal content, including government reports and briefings.
Less formal content may use exclamation marks sparingly.
An exclamation mark displayed as a literal character, such as in password instructions, is not emphatic punctuation.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates the heading and introductory restriction; G-2 records the informal-content and literal-character qualifications.

covers.quote: Don’t use exclamation marks too often.

parts.quote: Congratulations to our 2020 Australia Day Award recipients!
Happy international mother language day! #ourAPS believes in the importance of cultural and linguistic diversity (CALD) for a sustainable and harmonious Australian society.

rules.quote: Use them sparingly in less formal content such as promotional material and social media posts.
rules.specification: The page gives no numerical threshold for ‘sparingly’ or ‘too often’. A frequency threshold would require a reviewer’s decision; occasional use is not itself a violation.
rules.violation_condition: Exclamation marks occur too frequently in less formal government content.
when: Applies to less formal government content, including promotional material and social media posts.
Formal content is subject to the separate restriction on using exclamation marks at all.
rules.why: G-4 merges the two statements of the frequency restriction; G-1 keeps frequency separate from multiple marks at one sentence ending.

covers.quote: Some people use multiple exclamation marks in social media. This is not suitable for government content.

parts.quote: Were you born overseas or have a parent who was? Nearly half of Australians do!
Were you born overseas or have a parent who was? Nearly half of Australians do!!!

rules.quote: At the end of each sentence you want to emphasise, use only one exclamation mark.
rules.violation_condition: A sentence ends with more than one exclamation mark used for emphasis.
when: Applies when exclamation marks are used to emphasise a sentence.
Applies to government social media content as well as other government content.
Does not apply to exclamation marks displayed as literal characters rather than sentence punctuation.
rules.why: G-1 separates the heading’s frequency and sentence-ending checks; G-2 and G-4 absorb the social-media clarification.
